_readme.what: Complete results from an evaluation of 154 public college-football computer models against the betting market, 2001-2025.
_readme.why: Handed to an outside reviewer for methodological critique. Everything needed to judge the analysis is in this file; no repo access required.
read_this_first: Loss is MSE in points-squared. NEGATIVE d_vs_r0 = BETTER than the benchmark.
Every number here is POST-FIX. Five specification defects were found during the analysis (see defects_found); all headline numbers were recomputed.
Two benchmarks are reported separately and the answer differs completely between them. This IS the main finding.
The bootstrap p-value floor is 1/2000 = 0.0005. A reported p of 0.000 means 'below the floor', not zero. Do not quote corrected p-values to six decimals.
Method codes are E4-E14; see method_catalog for what each one is.
_readme.headline: The panel decisively beats the OPENING line and cannot beat the CLOSING line by any of ten combination rules. Best closing-line Holm-adjusted p is 0.4865.

panel.burn_in: seasons through 2005 train only; 20 evaluated seasons
panel.unbalanced: Models enter and exit. At 2025, 39 of 154 were active.

protocol.validation: Nested walk-forward. Train on all prior seasons, predict the next. Hyperparameters chosen on an inner split (last 3 training seasons) by the 1-SE rule, so selection never sees the evaluated season.
protocol.anchoring: Every method is anchored on R0 by Frisch-Waugh, so all nest the benchmark and a zero correction returns R0 exactly. Verified by test to 1e-8.
protocol.inference: Wild cluster bootstrap-t, Rademacher weights, null imposed by centring, clustered by season. B=2000, 25 clusters.
protocol.multiplicity: Holm within the 8-member exploratory family E7-E14, per benchmark. E4 and E6 are outside the family (E4 pre-registered, E6 a repair).
protocol.preregistration: E6-E14 with named grids and the conservative direction of each were committed BEFORE any fitting.

method_catalog.mkt: The raw market line (opening or closing), used as published.
method_catalog.R0: Recalibrated line. OLS of margin on [1, line], refit each season on prior seasons. THE BENCHMARK: every method below is anchored on it by Frisch-Waugh, so all of them nest it and a zero correction lands on R0 exactly.
method_catalog.E4: Screened equal-weighted consensus. Take the K=20 models with the best prior-season market-relative skill, average their deviations from the line, fit one scalar gamma. K was fixed at 20 BEFORE any fitting.
method_catalog.E6: Market-residual ridge. Ridge of (y - mkt) on all active models' deviations.
method_catalog.E7: E4 with K chosen out-of-sample by the 1-SE rule instead of fixed at 20.
method_catalog.E8: Stock-Watson generalized shrinkage. Fit the unrestricted correction, shrink it toward zero by a scalar psi.
method_catalog.E9: Market-residual principal components. Regress (y - mkt) on the first r scores.
method_catalog.E10: Market-anchored peLASSO. LASSO-select a subset, equal-weight survivors, one gamma.
method_catalog.E11: Trimmed residual consensus. Drop top and bottom tau per game, average the rest.
method_catalog.E12: Combination elastic net. E6 with an l1+l2 penalty.
method_catalog.E13: Online residual aggregation. Hedge-style exponential weights updated per game.
method_catalog.E14: Complete subset regression after screening. Screen to the 10 best by prior-season residual skill, average all C(10,k) k-variable residual regressions. k=1 was selected in every season.

harvey_newbold_encompassing._what: Joint encompassing: does the line encompass the panel as a SET? Five PRE-SPECIFIED directions, not a 154-dim Wald that would have no power. Null imposed by centring, season-clustered wild bootstrap calibrates it. IN-SAMPLE by construction (the PCA and the screen both use the whole panel) -- that is the standard framing for an encompassing test, which asks about the population, not about out-of-sample deployability.
harvey_newbold_encompassing._reading: line does NOT encompass the panel

e6_vs_e5_repair._what: E6 (ridge) vs E5 (the parent unrestricted combination) on their own paired support. E6 was pre-registered as a REPAIR of E5, not an exploratory method, so it carries no Holm correction.

leaderboard_top25.NOT_A_MODEL: This column is a market line, not a forecasting model. Its skill is not model skill. Do not cite it.

opening._leaderboard_caveat: Single-model skill, NOT the combination results. Ranked by delta_mse vs the raw line (negative = better). Rows flagged NOT_A_MODEL are market lines and must not be read as forecasting skill. NOTE: once those two are removed, EVERY remaining model is worse than the raw line -- the best (lineespn) by +4.88 MSE. 'The two best forecasters' elsewhere in this file means best AMONG MODELS, not better than the market. The panel only beats the line in combination, never individually.

column_glossary.d_vs_r0: mean paired MSE difference vs the recalibrated benchmark; NEGATIVE is better
column_glossary.p: wild cluster bootstrap-t two-sided p, unadjusted
column_glossary.p_holm: Holm-adjusted within the 8-member exploratory family; null = outside it
column_glossary.frac_seasons: fraction of the 20 evaluated seasons the method beat R0
column_glossary.mean_abs_corr: mean |prediction - R0|; how far the method actually moves off its own reference. Near zero = the selected hyperparameter switched the correction OFF, so the method IS R0.
column_glossary.sign_stab: KNOWN INERT, see defect 7. Bounded below at 0.50.
column_glossary.rmse_mkt_same_games: the market RMSE on THIS method games, so a reduced-support method is not compared against a different game set
column_glossary.viable: yes / NO / none, from the stability gate; 'none' = degenerate

recency_and_cohort.question: Does exponentially discounting old market-relative losses, or adjusting for entry cohort, improve the screen? Validation was to determine the decay rate rather than declaring a structural break.
recency_and_cohort.answer: No. rho=1.00 (no decay) won 20/20 seasons on both benchmarks. Giacomini-Rossi finds no instability. The cohort correction DESTROYS signal because the best forecasters are recent entrants.

market_contamination.what: Two panel columns (lineca, linemidweek) proved to BE market lines, not models. This check drops the 15 most market-like columns and refits.
market_contamination.note: Retention is the fraction of the original effect that survives.
market_contamination.closing_line_lead: On the CLOSING line E14 strengthens under decontamination: -0.159 (p=0.0695) becomes -0.193 [-0.344,-0.045] p=0.0125. This is a post-hoc variant of the winner of an eight-member family with no confirmation window. Holm across that family puts it near 0.10. A candidate for pre-registration, NOT a closing-line edge.

akm_bound.problem: E14 was the SELECTED method among 8, so its effect is conditional on having won a noisy tournament.
akm_bound.approach: Andrews-Kitagawa-McCloskey is the right framework, but implementing it literally needs an 8x8 cluster-robust covariance not persisted by the sweep. Bounded instead: the correction is E[max_m Z] * se * sqrt(1-rho), and BOTH unknowns (rho, effective m) only ever shrink it. The rho=0 corner is a valid worst case.

inputs.se_note: half-width / 1.96. Real bootstrap-t quantiles at 20 clusters are fatter, implying a SMALLER se and LARGER z, so this is the reading least favourable to the finding.

akm_bound.conclusion: Worst case over the entire rho range leaves p = 2.4e-4, still under the bootstrap 1/2000 floor, and the effect no weaker than -1.88. Two of the eight candidates were degenerate on opening (E8 |corr|=0.03, E12=0.17) and could not have won, so effective m is 6 and the bound tightens to 1.3e-4.
cautions: The correction REPLACES Holm rather than stacking with it.
Both raw and corrected p sit below the bootstrap floor, so the honest statement is 'below 1/2000 before and after winner correction'.
AKM real bite is on the POINT ESTIMATE, not the p-value.

defects_found.detail: spreads passed to a function taking margins
defects_found.consequence: An absurd +23 adjusted mean where the correct value is +0.45.

defects_found.defect: Methods did not nest the benchmark
defects_found.detail: fitting y-mkt ~ deviations pins the market coefficient at 1
defects_found.consequence: Every comparison against R0, Clark-West included, formally invalid. Rebuilt on Frisch-Waugh anchoring with a test asserting 1e-8 equivalence.

defects_found.detail: one method that cannot fit before ~2011 silently deleted those seasons for every other method
defects_found.consequence: n fell 14347 -> 9234 with no indication why.

defects_found.defect: Coverage filter was a tenure test
defects_found.detail: coverage measured over the whole training history, so a model launched in 2015 could never qualify however complete its record
defects_found.consequence: Regression methods fit on ~14 old models rather than the season's ~39 active ones, EXCLUDING THE TWO BEST FORECASTERS. Changed every headline in the regression family.

defects_found.detail: while its bootstrap imposed the null by centring
defects_found.consequence: Tested 'is the difference nonzero', not 'does it change over time'.

defects_found.detail: a reduced-support method printed beside the shared market RMSE
defects_found.consequence: Reproduced the coverage-difficulty confound inside a doc explaining that confound.

defects_found.detail: sign_stability is bounded below at 0.50 and returns 1.00 for a consistently tiny coefficient
defects_found.consequence: The gate was one criterion, not two. Recorded, not retrofitted.

preregistration_scorecard.summary: Eight expectations were committed before fitting. FOUR WERE WRONG.

rows.expectation: K-by-rule will score worse than K=20, exposing the latter as selection-inflated
rows.detail: the rule chose 'all' in 20/20 seasons -- K is not identifiable out-of-sample at all

rows.expectation: Market-residual ridge beats E5, still not R0
rows.detail: it beats R0 on opening, and is significantly WORSE than both on closing

rows.expectation: Online aggregation and CSR will not help
rows.detail: CSR was the only exploratory method to survive Holm, on full support, p<0.0001, beating the reference in all 20 seasons

rows.expectation: No method passes the stability gate
rows.detail: seven did, and the gate was weaker than designed (defect 7)

rows.expectation: rho=1.00 selected in a majority of seasons
No recency scheme changes the closing-line null
Giacomini-Rossi rejects on opening, not closing
rows.detail: rejects on neither; the open/close gap is a difference in level, not drift over time

rows.expectation: Cohort trend small, will not reorder the screen
rows.detail: the correction destroys signal because the best forecasters are recent entrants

known_limitations: No confirmation window exists. The 2021-25 minimum detectable effect is 0.161 RMSE against a full-window 0.078, so a holdout cannot confirm an effect this size.

Prediction Tracker publishes mid-week with no publication timestamp, so it is unknown what price was available when a forecast appeared. The opening-line edge is an UNREACHABLE UPPER BOUND, not a strategy.

25 season clusters is below the ~40 where analytic cluster SEs can be trusted; wild cluster bootstrap-t with Rademacher weights and the null imposed by centring is the primary inference. B=2000, so the p-value floor is 1/2000 = 0.0005.
Missingness is almost certainly not at random: models enter and exit, and coverage correlates with game difficulty.
sign_stability is inert (defect 7), so the viability gate is one criterion, not two.
The pairwise correlation structure across the 8 candidate methods was never measured; the AKM bound below is constructed so that it does not need to be.
open_questions: Selection-adjusted inference with no confirmation window (see akm_bound -- believed closed by bound, would like this confirmed or refuted).
Why did complete subset regression survive when every shrinkage estimator did not? Is CSR at k=1 effectively an equal-weighted average of many one-regressor corrections?
Is the 1-SE rule the wrong selection rule for a SMALL correction to a STRONG benchmark? It always picks the more conservative end, which here means 'do nothing'.
Benchmark contamination inside forecast panels -- is there a named detection method?
4b. Why does an equal-weighted consensus resist contamination that a ridge amplifies (73% vs 27% retention)? Is there a diagnostic that finds this WITHOUT already having a contamination measure?
When does cohort/vintage adjustment destroy signal rather than confounding?

5b. Eligibility rules in unbalanced forecaster panels -- my filter silently became a tenure test, and eligibility correlated with entry year almost perfectly, which is the same confound the cohort correction was meant to address.
Detecting slow decay in relative performance with ~20 time-series observations.
Is squared error the right loss for a betting decision (which is a sign/threshold call)?
Which market number is the right benchmark?
Does closing line value actually predict realised profitability?
Persistent skill without exploitable edge -- the mutual-fund analogy.
